## Species We Study

::: {.gallery}

![Gray treefrogs (*Hyla versicolor*) are an ideal species to study photoperiod and thermal physiology. They are also one of the cutest amphbians!](images/field-notes/gray-treefrog.jpg){.lightbox}

![Western spadefoot toad juvenile (*Pelobates cultripes*) used in research on light pollution, photoperiod, and temperature in Spain.](images/field-notes/spadefoot.jpg){.lightbox}

![American toads (*Anaxyrus americanus*) are widely distributed across urban environments and could be an ideal species to study.](images/field-notes/toad.jpg){.lightbox}

![American bullfrog (*Rana catesbeiana*) are commonly found in ponds in Ohio.](images/field-notes/bullfrog.jpg){.lightbox}

![Spring peepers (*Pseudacris crucifer*) are some of the earliest amphibians to breed in the spring; they make that iconic high-pitched peep!.](images/field-notes/peeper.jpg){.lightbox}

![Green frogs (*Rana clamitans*) make that banjo sound that you hear around the pond.](images/field-notes/green-frog.jpg){.lightbox}

:::
